properties.title: Flood Advisory issued September 14 at 10:45PM MDT until September 15 at 12:45AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Mesa County in west central Colorado near
Whitewater...

* WHEN...Until 1245 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1045 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This will cause arroyo and small stream flooding
possible mud over the area roadways. Overflowing poor drainage
areas will cause minor flooding in the advisory area. Between 0.3
and 0.6 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Indian Creek, Gunnison River, Rapid Creek, Colorado River, Big
Beaver Creek, Mesa Creek, Whitewater Creek, Sink Creek, East
Creek and Kannah Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Whitewater and areas near Kanah Creek.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 14 at 9:25PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
At 925 PM MST, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Florence Junction, or 9 miles north of Florence, moving northeast at
10 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Florence Junction and Queen Valley.

This includes the following highways...
US Highway 60 between mile markers 212 and 215.
AZ Route 79 between mile markers 141 and 150.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.
properties.area: Northwest Pinal County; Apache Junction/Gold Canyon

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued September 14 at 9:11PM MST until September 14 at 11:30PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Pima County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 1130 PM MST.

* At 911 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms had produced heavy rain in Brawley Wash at Manville
Road. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Avra Valley, Saguaro National Park West and Picture Rocks.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Manville Rd at Brawley Wash and Twin Peaks Rd between Sanders and
Sandario.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 14 at 9:25PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Citrus and Levy
Counties.

.Elevated water levels are expected along the river over the next
several days due to recent heavy rainfall.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 PM EDT Monday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue rising to 28.2 feet just
after midnight tonight. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.4
feet on 08/05/2024.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday afternoon at 200 PM EDT.
properties.area: Citrus, FL; Levy, FL; Marion, FL

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 14 at 9:23PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Horse Creek near Arcadia at SR 72.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The access road to Hidden Oak is
impassable.

Wednesday morning and continue rising to 12.4 feet Thursday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.5
feet on 08/31/2002.
